Quirky Subaru SVX Grand Tourer Comes Back to Virtual Life Based on the Subaru Sport Mobility Concept
10 photos
Photo: Theottle / YouTube
The Japanese automaker Subaru is extremely beloved in places like North America, especially the United States. As such, we weren’t surprised to see the local division recovering from the slump from earlier this year.
The folks over from Subaru are slowly but steadily coming back to positive results – October 2026 saw a six percent increase across the US automotive market to 54k units, with sales led by Crosstrek and Forester going up by 26% both during the month. Even the WRX is up by 55% year-to-date, but Subaru of America needs a continued punch to come out of the woods: year-to-date total deliveries are now almost 530k units, down close to one percent from last year.
You can’t say they’re not taking measures. For example, the 2027 Subaru Outback has become more affordable than last year, starting at $32,995 MSRP instead of almost $35k, thanks to the new model year bringing with it a fresh entry-level model. Additionally, we heard that Subie made an in-house EV packing 510 hp and featuring Aisin drive units plus Panasonic battery cells, skipping the usual cooperation with Toyota.
However, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI because they have a fresh proposal: this virtual artist, better known as " Theottle " on social media, has resorted to CGI slicing and dicing an older concept to make a fresh Subaru GT coupe for the lineup.
It makes sense: Subaru only sells the Impreza compact five-door hatchback, BRZ RWD entry-level sports car, and the WRX compact sports sedan in America, so a range-topping passenger car might also fit in for the right price and with the right characteristics.
His proposal is quite simple: bring back the quirky Subaru SVX nameplate, a two-door grand tourer with four-wheel drive produced from 199 through 1996 with a 3.3-liter boxer-six engine. This pixel master’s vision includes the defunct Audi A5 coupe as the placeholder for the unofficial, hypothetical SVX design project in his latest behind-the-scenes making-of video, and for the styling he used the cool Subaru Sport Mobility Concept all-electric sports coupe presented at the 2023 Japan Mobility Show.
The model was Subie’s vision for all-electric performance at the time, and he remembered it and now set out to imagine its production-ready version as a next-generation Subaru SVX. Naturally, the CGI expert didn’t forget about “SVX’s most distinctive design cue: its signature window-within-a-window glass design.”
So, what do you think – yay or nay? Should they make something like this and risk a potential failure in the US, where EVs aren’t beloved at the moment, or hope that if they fit it with that new EV powertrain, it will turn into a worthy successor to Subaru’s iconic 1990s grand touring coupe?
